PullRequest.Title: github: harden request execution and add client attribution
PullRequest.Body:
Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678.

Harden the existing reusable GitHub engine ahead of the broader request-consolidation work:

- Bound retained requests, coalesced waiters, response sizes, and end-to-end request lifetimes; add caller fairness and reserved admission capacity for interactive/mutation work.
- Preserve rate-limit cooldowns across invalidation and identity-bootstrap failures, classify bounded download diagnostics, and recheck cooldowns before authenticated redirect hops. Keep writes non-retrying except for existing operation-specific reconciliation.
- Add privacy-safe request health summaries and sampled timings using product telemetry, with bounded categories and no request/account/repository content.
- Add binding-supplied product/component identification and per-attempt retry headers. Node egress sends all four headers; browser fetch (including desktop renderers) sends only the CORS-allowed `X-Client-Application` to `api.github.com`. Enterprise browser identification remains disabled until its header contracts are confirmed. Storage redirects receive no identification or retry headers.
- Add deterministic regression coverage and source-adjacent architecture/behavior documentation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench and Agent Host repository/issue/PR hydration, polling, refresh, and pagination
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold request waits for credential identity resolution, admission/cooldown, the GitHub REST or GraphQL response, bounded body decoding, and parsing. Warm credential, ETag, and in-flight-coalesced paths skip identity or duplicate wire work. Telemetry aggregation is not a blocking boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared request per credential generation; concurrent credential callers await the same identity promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same identity lookup was already required; the diff adds a deadline, caller attribution, cooldown preservation, and cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required on a cold or replaced credential before repository requests can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue GitHub REST or GraphQL reads and consume bounded responses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One wire operation per distinct effective REST/GraphQL key after in-flight coalescing, with pagination remaining one request per page up to existing page caps; reads can make one existing bounded retry on transient failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same REST/GraphQL boundaries, ETag revalidation, coalescing, pagination, and read retry existed; the diff bounds retained work and response bytes and changes scheduling/metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each required fragment/page is on that fragment's refresh path; independent fragment requests are governed by the shared queue.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active resource subscriptions, requested PR fragments, and bounded pagination pages; equivalent reads collapse to one wire request with at most 64 waiters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changed queue caps four active requests globally, two per host, two per caller, and one per account; cooldown-waiting work consumes no active slot. Same-key reads coalesce, while account-level serialization limits the common single-account case to one active network request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Credentials and host capabilities share in-flight work; REST uses a 500-entry ETag LRU; identical REST/GraphQL reads coalesce. Cold cache performs network work, warm ETag reads still revalidate, and failures do not remain in the coalescing maps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and bounds from transport, queue, resource-service cancellation, and lifecycle tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual fragment counts and response sizes vary by PR and subscription visibility, but all changed retention, waiter, response, and concurrency dimensions are explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff does not add per-item network fan-out, and its extra scheduling, response-bound, metadata, and telemetry work is bounded relative to existing network requests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive PR mutations, reconciliation, workflow reruns, and workflow-log downloads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mutations wait for credential resolution, per-repository serialization, queue admission, and one write attempt. Only ambiguous dispatched failures enter existing operation-specific reconciliation. Downloads wait for queue/cooldown, redirect hops, and bounded body consumption.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send REST or GraphQL mutation writes and, for ambiguous outcomes, refresh authoritative state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport attempt per write; no automatic transport retry. Reconciliation is failure-only and bounded by the operation-specific workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Writes and operation-specific reconciliation already crossed the network; the diff extends ambiguity classification to newly bounded timeout/oversize outcomes without blindly replaying transport mutations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write is on the user action's critical path; reconciliation runs only after an ambiguous dispatched result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch a workflow log through at most five redirects and read a bounded body
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial request plus at most five redirect hops per explicit download; no retry. Authenticated 403 diagnostics consume at most 8 KiB.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Downloads and redirect hops already existed; the diff moves them under common admission/deadlines, strips metadata cross-origin, and bounds diagnostic and successful response reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All hops and body reading are on the explicit download path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User-triggered mutation count, bounded reconciliation attempts after ambiguous failures, redirect count capped at five, and requested download bytes capped by both the operation and 16 MiB transport maximum.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutations retain high-priority/reserved admission and are serialized by existing repository operation logic; transport still permits one active request per account. Downloads share the same global/host/account queue and are not retried.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Writes bypass read coalescing and ETags. Workflow status reads may use the existing REST cache; downloads are no-store. Cooldowns are preserved across credential invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from mutation service branches, transport retry policy, and lifecycle tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Ambiguous failures and long redirect chains are uncommon and environment-dependent, but their new work is bounded and failure-only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new unbounded replay or fan-out is introduced, and the small 403 diagnostic read is capped at 8 KiB.

Scenarios.Scenario: Credential replacement, identity bootstrap failures, and rate-limit cooldown recovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Token acquisition and a cold /user lookup are critical. Server cooldown waits are parked before active admission, and each credential caller has a five-minute end-to-end deadline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the GitHub account identity after token acquisition or replacement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared /user request per credential generation; failed subsequent generations wait for preserved Retry-After/backoff rather than burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identity resolution already performed /user; the diff prevents repeated attempts during server cooldowns and bounds stalled token/identity waits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks authenticated GitHub work until identity is known; cooldown waits occur before the next network attempt.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Credential generations and concurrent callers; callers share generation work while token rotation invalidates the old generation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One identity promise per generation; callers have independent deadlines. Cooldown-waiting requests occupy retained admission but no active network slot.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful identity is cached for the current generation. Failures back off; server cooldown is transferred out of the transient bootstrap account and inactive quota state is removed after expiry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from credential, backoff, coordinator, and deterministic scheduler tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Token churn and rate-limit prevalence vary, but the changed behavior reduces rather than increases retry cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff coalesces and delays boundary work and adds bounded cleanup rather than increasing network attempts.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Header construction and counter/sample updates run synchronously per admitted logical request or wire attempt. A five-minute flush or service disposal emits one summary and at most ten timing events; emission is not awaited by GitHub requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit aggregated product telemetry events through ITelemetryService.publicLog2
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only for active windows: one summary plus at most ten reservoir samples every five minutes or on disposal; idle engines emit nothing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No GitHub request-health summary or timing events were emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Flush is timer/disposal-driven and off the GitHub request critical path; per-request work is fixed-size counters and a reservoir update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing GitHub requests with bounded attribution headers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional calls; fixed headers are added to each existing eligible wire attempt, with browser egress limited to one header.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The network calls already occurred without these attribution headers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Header construction precedes the existing fetch but adds no round trip or serialization proportional to request content.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Logical request and wire-attempt frequency within each five-minute window; retained timing samples stay capped at ten regardless of traffic volume.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Telemetry does not create concurrent GitHub requests. Flush emits a bounded sequence through the telemetry service, while GitHub request concurrency remains queue-controlled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Aggregation is window-local, reset after flush, discarded immediately when telemetry is disabled, and does not cache request/account/repository content.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the collector implementation and flood/opt-out tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry service internals may buffer or transmit later, but this diff invokes it at a fixed maximum of eleven events per active window.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the introduced work is fixed per request, retained state is bounded, and emission cardinality is capped independently of request volume.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancellation, resource dormancy, timeout, and service shutdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resource disposal/dormancy, waiter cancellation, credential replacement, and deadlines abort the propagated signal; callers reject immediately and replacement work can be admitted. Underlying browser and Agent Host fetch adapters receive the abort signal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Abort active fetches and admit replacement GitHub requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Active queue occupancy is capped at four, with one per account. Cancelled logical work is removed immediately; production fetch implementations receive the abort signal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old queue retained active occupancy until the task promise settled; the changed queue rejects and releases capacity synchronously after signaling abort.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cancellation is off the abandoned request's success path and permits current user-visible work to proceed without waiting for an obsolete request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency of resource interest changes, credential invalidations, and deadlines while requests are active.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The queue admits replacements immediately after abort. Browser fetch and the Agent Host proxy-patched global fetch receive the queue controller signal, so no concrete sustained concurrency beyond abort settlement was established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cancelled waiters detach immediately; when the last waiter leaves, the shared map entry is removed and its controller is aborted. Rejected unique reads do not retain coalescing entries or waiter timers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in immediate logical release and signal propagation; insufficient evidence that production adapters ignore abort long enough to create a material burst.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Physical socket teardown may lag JavaScript abort settlement, but repository adapters are abort-aware and there is no evidence of realistic accumulated live requests or retained tasks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although release moved earlier, the diff propagates abort through both production egress paths and no concrete user-visible concurrency or retention regression is established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 34 changed files and full paginated diffs. Traced request admission, coalescing, retries, rate-limit parking, response buffering, cancellation, credential lifecycle, downloads, mutations, and telemetry. No high-confidence actionable performance regression introduced by the diff was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
